dcf.method: 5-year FCFF: EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital; growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate; Gordon terminal value; equity = EV - borrowings.

blocks.text: Tempsens designs and makes engineered, made-to-order thermal products in three verticals: temperature sensing solutions (thermocouples, RTDs, infrared pyrometers, online thermal imagers), specialised cables (high-temperature instrumentation and control cables, LV power cables, mineral-insulated metal-sheathed cables, nickel alloy conductors) and electrical heating solutions (process and component heaters, laboratory and process furnaces, and now medium-voltage heaters) [F] (PPT Sep 2026). FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 444.88 crore, with the vertical mix at 44.59% sensing, 34.71% cables and 20.70% heating [F] (PPT Sep 2026). It makes money by selling engineered products into new projects and OEM programmes (67.55% of FY26 revenue) and into replacement/MRO demand (32.45%) [F] (PPT Sep 2026).

End markets in FY26: petrochemical 21.45%, metal 19.68%, power 12.27%, others 9.99%, traders 9.58%, manufacturers 9.42%, defence & nuclear 6.95%, glass 6.74%, plastic 3.90% [F] (PPT Sep 2026). Geography: India 71.48% and exports 28.52% of FY26 revenue, sold to 80+ countries [F] (PPT Sep 2026). In Q1 FY27 exports rose to about 34% of product revenue, partly because newly acquired European subsidiaries were consolidated [F] (PPT Sep 2026). The customer base is fragmented: the top 10 customers were 18.59% of FY26 revenue, down from 24.74% in FY24 [F] (PPT Sep 2026).

Listing status: Tempsens listed on NSE and BSE on 28 August 2026 through a Rs 650 crore IPO priced at Rs 300 (Rs 95 crore fresh issue, Rs 555 crore offer for sale) [F] (BOARD). Q1 FY27 was its first earnings call as a listed company [F] (CALL Sep 2026). The evidence base is thin. We have no annual report, no prospectus in the folder, no audit report, no related-party note and no credit-rating rationale text (the ICRA page was only a log-in shell) [F] (RATING). Historical statements are 'restated' IPO financials [F] (PPT Sep 2026). Many forensic tests in this report therefore come back 'not disclosed in the documents available'.

blocks.text: Driver classification [AI]: theses 1 and 5 are company-specific; 2 and 3 are company-specific execution bets; 4 and 6 are structural (import substitution, electrification) but not proprietary to Tempsens; end-market demand from steel, petrochemical and power is cyclical and underlies all of them.

items: 1. Valuation is far above every DCF scenario. The price is Rs 494 against per-share values of Rs 34 (bear), Rs 63.8 (base) and Rs 92.6 (bull). The reverse DCF implies 107.9% annual sales growth for five years, against 17.2% in the base case [F] (NUMBERS).

2. Headline growth is partly acquired. The FY24-26 revenue CAGR of 27.23% 'incorporates the effect' of consolidating Marathon Heater for the full year in FY25 [F] (PPT Sep 2026). Heating went from 3.90% of revenue in FY24 to 20.70% in FY26 [F] (PPT Sep 2026). We estimate sensing plus cables grew about 15% a year over FY24-26 [E] (PPT Sep 2026).

3. Q1 FY27 growth is also not like-for-like. It includes Tempsens Germany, Tempsens Polska and Tempsens Measurement & Control, and 'prior-period figures are not restated' [F] (PPT Sep 2026). Organic growth is not disclosed.
4. Cash conversion is weak and getting worse. CFO/PAT was 0.59 in FY26 and 0.71 cumulatively over five years. The cash conversion cycle widened from 151 days (FY24) to 210 days (FY26) [F] (NUMBERS).

5. Margins fell in the first listed quarter. Operating margin was 20% in Q1 FY27 against 23% in Q1 FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). Employee cost rose 45% [F] (CALL Sep 2026). PAT grew only 15.6% on 33.4% revenue growth [F] (PPT Sep 2026).
6. Returns have diluted. ROCE fell from 36% (FY22) to 18% (FY26) and ROE from 32.3% to 15.3% [F] (NUMBERS). Goodwill and intangibles of Rs 154.7 crore are 23% of FY26 total assets [F] (PPT Sep 2026).

7. The company favours adjusted metrics. Its EBITDA includes other income and the JV share. Adjusted PAT excludes acquisition amortisation. Adjusted ROE deducts goodwill from equity (23.08% versus 15.3% reported) [F] (PPT Sep 2026) [F] (NUMBERS).
8. No order book is disclosed. Management describes it only as '4, 4.5 months' typical and a 'solid order book' [MC] (CALL Sep 2026).
9. The IPO was mostly an exit. Rs 555 crore of the Rs 650 crore issue was an offer for sale [F] (BOARD). Lock-in expiries are a supply overhang (dates not in the documents) [AI].
10. The forensic basics are missing. Related-party transactions, contingent liabilities, auditor, KAMs and CARO are not in the documents available, so they cannot be cleared.

Is 25% growth organic? Management guides FY27 growth 'in line with' the blended 3-year growth [MC] (CALL Sep 2026). Screener's 3-year sales CAGR is 22.9% [F] (NUMBERS). The market may be paying for acquired growth as if it were organic, or it may be underrating the new-capacity step-up [AI].

Is the Q1 margin dip temporary? Management attributes about 140 bp to employee cost invested ahead of growth and expects recovery in H2 [MC] (CALL Sep 2026). Gross margin at 47.4% was in line with FY25/FY26 [F] (PPT Sep 2026). Whether this is a step-up in the fixed-cost base or a timing issue will show in Q2-Q3 [AI].

Is the DCF too punitive? The model's capex rule uses a fixed-asset turnover of 1.49 [F] (NUMBERS). Screener's fixed assets of Rs 299 crore appear to include Rs 154.7 crore of goodwill and intangibles [E] (PPT Sep 2026), so growth capex may be overstated. Even so, the bull value is 81% below the price [F] (NUMBERS).

Is the moat narrow or broad? Being the sole Indian non-contact maker covers about a tenth of revenue [E] (BOARD). The other ~90% competes with WIKA, Endress+Hauser, Radix and Pyroelectric [F] (BOARD).

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus story is 'Indian thermal-engineering compounder with a capacity doubling ahead'. Our reading is narrower. The operating business is a qualification-protected, fragmented-customer niche that grew about 15% a year organically in sensing and cables over FY24-26 [E] (PPT Sep 2026). On top of that sit an acquired heating platform and newly consolidated European subsidiaries that flatter reported growth. Working capital absorbs most incremental profit. At Rs 494 the price discounts sustained hyper-growth that even the bull DCF does not reach [F] (NUMBERS). The upside variant is real but unproven: OEM contracts, MV heaters and the Rs 500 crore capacity pipeline could change the growth algorithm from FY28. None of them is quantified as an order today.

[AI] The core sensing and cables franchise is 20-35 years old and organically built. The current three-vertical shape is much newer. Heating became material only through the FY25 Marathon amalgamation. The European subsidiaries, Tempsens Measurement & Control, the Victura JV, the Mexico entity and the OEM programmes all date from 2025-26. At least a fifth of revenue and most of the forward growth narrative therefore have a track record of under two years, and none of it under listed-company disclosure.

blocks.text: Gross material margin was 46.0% in FY26 and 46.9% in FY25 [E] (PPT Sep 2026), against 39.2% in FY24 [E] (PPT Sep 2026). We calculate these as revenue less materials consumed and the change in inventories. Management attributes the level to 'engineering content' [MC] (CALL Sep 2026). [AI] Value is captured at engineering, qualification and integration, not at material conversion. The 7.7 pp gross-margin jump in FY25 coincides with the Marathon amalgamation, which suggests heating carries a higher gross margin, offset by higher employee cost (employee cost rose from 10.9% of revenue in FY24 to 14.3% in FY26) [E] (PPT Sep 2026). Segment margins are not disclosed. Management says sensing and heating margins are 'slightly more' than cables [MC] (CALL Sep 2026).

Outsourcing is not disclosed. Hard assets (PPE, right-of-use assets and CWIP) were Rs 145.4 crore at FY26 against Rs 444.9 crore of revenue, about 3.1x hard-asset turnover [E] (PPT Sep 2026). Capex/sales averaged 7.4% over FY22-26 [E] (NUMBERS). [AI] On fixed capital this is moderately asset-light. On working capital it is heavy: CCC was 210 days in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: FY26 unrealised FX gain was Rs 1.41 crore [F] (PPT Sep 2026). Hedging policy is not disclosed. Tariff exposure: no dated tariff or trade-policy event is discussed in the documents. The call says 'We operate 15 manufacturing plants, five of them in India, five of them outside India', and later refers to 'six location outside India' [MC] (CALL Sep 2026). We have not reconciled these.

The only utilisation figure is a verbal 'about 80%' for existing capacity, with plants usually run 'at about 80% at max' [MC] (CALL Sep 2026). No trend is disclosed. [AI] Taken together, these remarks imply existing plants are close to practical full capacity, so growth beyond FY27 depends on the new projects. Sensitivity, not base case: if FY26 revenue of Rs 445 crore was produced at 80%, theoretical 100% output would be about Rs 556 crore [E]. Management says it does not run there.

New capacity: Rs ~500 crore aggregate peak revenue at full utilisation [MC] (CALL Sep 2026). At management's own 80% practical ceiling that is about Rs 400 crore [E]. Full utilisation is expected 'broadly' by end-FY29/start-FY30 [MC] (CALL Sep 2026). Lease expiries: right-of-use assets were Rs 31.2 crore at FY26 [F] (PPT Sep 2026); lease terms and lessors are not disclosed.

Capex and ratios [F] (NUMBERS); capex/EBITDA [E] (NUMBERS). Company cash flow: PPE payments of Rs 14.9 / 27.7 / 14.0 crore plus leasehold land of Rs 11.9 / 3.2 / 0 crore in FY24 / FY25 / FY26 [F] (PPT Sep 2026). Acquisitions are outside capex: Rs 0.85 crore (FY25) and Rs 15.23 crore (FY26) in cash [F] (PPT Sep 2026), plus the Marathon amalgamation settled in shares (FY25 share capital rose from Rs 1.85 crore to Rs 2.93 crore [F] (PPT Sep 2026)).

[E] From FY24 to FY26 revenue rose by Rs 170 crore. Hard assets (PPE plus right-of-use) rose by about Rs 45 crore, from Rs 99.4 crore to Rs 144.7 crore. Goodwill and intangibles rose by Rs 153.6 crore (PPT Sep 2026). On hard capital alone the incremental turnover is about 3.8x. Including acquired goodwill and intangibles it is about 0.85x. [AI] The organic business is asset-light, while the bought growth was capital-heavy.

Planned capex for the four projects is not disclosed, which is a significant gap. Known items: about Rs 25 crore of land for cables expansion bought in Q1 FY27 'from internal accruals' [F] (CALL Sep 2026), already twice FY26 capex. An agreement to acquire an 80,000 sq ft built shed for the Victura JV [MC] (CALL Sep 2026), value not disclosed. Fresh IPO proceeds: Rs 95 crore, of which Rs 55 crore went to debt repayment [F] (PPT Sep 2026). Use of the remaining Rs 40 crore is not stated in the documents. Classification [AI]: historically asset-light on fixed capital. FY27-28 will be capex-heavy relative to the FY26 run-rate.

Materials consumed were Rs 248.4 crore in FY26, 55.8% of revenue [F] (PPT Sep 2026). The documents do not itemise inputs, import dependence or source countries. The company makes 'our own alloys' and MI cable [MC] (CALL Sep 2026). [AI] Nickel alloys and thermocouple metals are likely key inputs, but the documents do not confirm this. Inventory was Rs 110-120 crore, 65-70% of it raw material [MC] (CALL Sep 2026); the balance sheet shows Rs 111.9 crore at FY26 [F] (PPT Sep 2026).

blocks.text: [AI] Reported profits are plausibly real, but conversion to cash is poor because inventory and receivables grow faster than sales. Earnings quality is moderate: there are no aggressive one-offs, but a structural cash-conversion gap.

Our DCF model is a 5-year FCFF projection. FCFF is EBITDA less tax on EBIT, less capex, less the change in net working capital. Growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate, and a Gordon terminal value follows [F] (NUMBERS). Base inputs: FY26 sales of Rs 445 crore, 23% EBITDA margin and 24.6% starting growth (median of 3-year, 5-year and TTM growth) fading to 10%. D&A is 3.1% of sales; capex equals depreciation plus new sales divided by fixed-asset turnover (1.49); working capital is 78 days; tax 25.2%; WACC 14.9%; terminal growth 5.5%; 8.383 crore shares [F] (NUMBERS).

[AI] The FY27E growth of 24.6% is consistent with management's 'blended 3-year growth' guidance [MC] (CALL Sep 2026). FCFF is negative in FY27-28 because the capex rule charges new sales at a 1.49x fixed-asset turnover and working capital at 78 days [F] (NUMBERS).

No disclosed peer multiples are available, so we make no relative-valuation comparison. [AI] Two features of the DCF matter. First, the capex rule uses a fixed-asset turnover of 1.49 [F] (NUMBERS); fixed assets appear to include Rs 154.7 crore of goodwill and intangibles [E] (PPT Sep 2026), so growth capex is likely overstated and DCF values likely understated. Second, WACC of 14.9% with 5.5% terminal growth is a demanding but standard hurdle. Neither feature can bridge a five-to-fifteen-fold gap. The market is pricing the stock on scarcity and on multiples for a newly listed thermal-engineering name, not on cash flows.

**The price requires about 107.9% annual sales growth for five years at the base margin, against 17.2% in the base case** [F] (NUMBERS). Historical growth: 3-year sales CAGR 22.9%, 5-year 26.4% [F] (NUMBERS). The bull case starts at 36.3% [F] (NUMBERS). [AI] Taken literally, revenue would need to reach roughly 39x FY26 within five years, which is far beyond even the Rs 500 crore peak capacity addition management describes [MC] (CALL Sep 2026).

[AI] Conclusion: on our model the price is not anchored to any cash-flow scenario the evidence supports. Counter-argument: the reverse DCF inherits the same goodwill-inflated capex rule and a 14.9% WACC. Long-duration Indian industrial niches have often traded at 50-60x earnings for years. If growth compounds at 20-25% for a decade, cash-flow models with 5-year fades will look too punitive. That is a duration bet, not something the documents demonstrate.

Tempsens is a real, profitable, qualification-protected niche manufacturer. Organic growth is in the mid-teens to low-20s, overlaid with acquisitions and a credible but unproven capacity and OEM expansion. At Rs 494 the shares trade at 58.3x FY26 earnings and 41.8x EBITDA, 5.3x the bull-case DCF value of Rs 92.6 and 7.7x the base value of Rs 63.8 [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. The gap comes from the market paying for long-duration scarcity and new-energy optionality that our cash-flow model, with its goodwill-heavy capex rule and 14.9% WACC, does not capture. The documents also do not yet evidence it. Investors with a multi-year horizon need to believe in growth well above the bull case. Re-review at Q2 FY27 results (organic growth, margin recovery, finance cost), at the FY27 annual report (RPT, auditor, contingent liabilities), and at the Q4 FY27-Q1 FY28 commissioning milestones.
